editorial.headline: Residential Estate Management: Open Nationally, Viable in Bali at Larger Scale
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the contracted management of residential property, from operations and repairs to budgets, charges and resident rules.
editorial.body:
Residential real-estate management under a fee or contract is the work of keeping a housing estate functioning as an organised whole. Its scope includes supervising and coordinating daily operations, maintenance and repairs; preparing and collecting residential charges; setting management budgets and income-and-expenditure plans; and drafting and enforcing residential rules. In practical terms, this is not the ownership or sale of homes, but the professional administration of the residential environment after the homes are in use.

The activity is open at micro, small, medium and large scale. That breadth matters because the code describes a management function rather than a single physical format of housing. A modest operation may coordinate routine upkeep and resident contributions, while a larger one may carry the fuller responsibility of operational oversight, planned maintenance, budget preparation and the enforcement of estate rules. Across those scales, the defining feature remains the same: management is delivered for a fee or under contract.

Nationally, this activity is open to foreign investment, up to a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The national position is therefore direct: a foreign-owned PMA business may enter this activity within that ceiling. There is no need to read a lower foreign-share cap into the record; the stated national maximum is full foreign ownership.

Bali requires a more precise reading, but it is not a prohibition. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High or High. Bali’s recorded status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, meaning the activity sits outside the moratorium’s blocked risk band rather than being barred for PMA registration. For founders, the useful conclusion is clear: national openness is matched by a Bali position that does not trigger the island-wide moratorium, with the stated risk treatment at large scale explaining why.
